answer: Vesting-latency escrow locks each new identity's payouts under a cipher until its signed history—the identity's fable—passes a quorum audit; a violet flag marks accounts during vesting. Each attempt costs a per-identity bond plus an admission fee, is capped at a few low-value tasks, and needs days of attested work before withdrawal. A coordinated ring fails because every fake identity must fund its own bond, wait the same latency, and cannot pool rewards without linking the addresses the escrow quarantines.
